quotes.excerpt: X-Men #34 is a strong character study of the Juggernaut, getting by on carefully crafted scriptwriting. With MacKay shifting to more solo stories as X-Men races toward DNX, here's hoping that he and future collaborators keep digging deep into what makes the X-Men tick.

X-Men #34 is a soft analysis of the current state of the Juggernaut rather than a deep dive into his character. The issue is meant to challenge him more than it’s meant to give any kind of exposé on the character’s past as a villain. All in all, it reads like something readers have seen before and is simple but has its nuance to a point.

This new story arc for the TMNT Universe is proving to be a challenge that they were warned would happen. I can understand wanting both of your parents back, but at the cost of New York City… This team continues to produce amazing issues every month with great action and storytelling. The added Chinese lore to this series is a joy to see. Seeing the Turtles engage in their heritage is something people should mimic. Take pride in your roots and where you come from. This is a great series and a great read for TMNT and non-TMNT fans.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #22 delivers an exciting escalation of The City That Never Dies, combining supernatural mystery, family consequences, and clear, atmospheric artwork. Gene Luen Yang, Fero Pe, and Luis Antonio Delgado turn Obon into the backdrop for a compelling catastrophe, leaving the Turtles facing a larger and more personal threat. It is a strong, fast-moving issue that builds anticipation for what comes next.

Conan The Barbarian #33 sets sail when Conan and the Red Brotherhood are shipwrecked on a mysterious island after encountering a massive storm and a supernatural attacker. Jim Zub’s start to the latest arc is as strong as ever, and Fernando Dagnino’s artwork is a perfect fit. 10 out of 10. No notes.

This is a ripping yard of piracy and sorcery, which highlights an often overlooked aspect of Conan’s background and the true character of Valeria of the Red Brotherhood. The artwork holds to the same standard of detail and drive. If you think of Conan as little more than a big, dumb barbarian, prepare to be educated!

Ultimately, A Mischief of Magpies is a haunting and beautiful book that goes far beyond merely being simply a solid fantasy. It’s an immersive story that resonates on so many levels. There’s a magic to this book that will break your heart—and it might be one of the best books to come out this year.
A Mischief Of Magpies #1 is perfection and sticks out as one of the best comics of the year so far. A must get.

Rick Remender and Daniel Acuna are on a generational run with Escape. This ninth chapter, which features a focus on Milton Shaw’s squadmate Flynn, delivers massive emotional moments and shows how quickly war can break even the strongest soldier down. There are some books that don’t match the hype that they generate, but this one surpasses it. Remender and Acuna continue to make magic.

The short narrative that opens the issue is hauntingly vivid. The stark simplicity of it serves as yet another example of just how well Escape is working. Overarching flat lines take a while to play out. So it can be difficult to tell exactly whether or not the creative team is going to be able to follow through on the potential of what they're setting up. Little, isolated narratives like the one at the beginning of the ninth issue show that they really are being very thoughtful about how everything is making it to the page. It's very striking stuff.

The Doom Patrol Issue 1 strips the team back and delivers incredible storytelling. What separates this group from many others in the DC Universe is clear, from the bonkers adventures to the lack of real leadership.

It's a promising start for a new series with one of the stranger superhero teams in mainstream comic books. It's not easy to bring them to the page in a way that feels like it's being true to their particular energy and personality. This particular creative team is doing a really good job of managing that much. It will be interesting to see where they move with it all as things progress. The first issue keeps it relatively simple. And variably it's going to get more complicated as such things as tended to with the Doom Patrol.

Space bandits Thena Khole and Cody Blue return in a new crossover series for the summer, Star-Crossed. Having stolen from a tyrannical monarchy, the girls just want to party. But any tyrant who’s been wronged is never going to let it go. And so the girls have a bounty on their heads they naively think they can escape. Best of luck, girls. From Mark Millar and Corrado Mastantuono.

Mark Millar delivers once again in this interstellar sci-fi outing any fan of the genre will love! Whether you’ve been following the Millarverse or not, this is one that any reader can easily get sucked into. Helped by the exceptional work of Corrado and Nisa Mastantuono, “Star-Crossed” is on its way to being one of the great modern sci-fi romps.

The Dirt Beneath the Devil #1 is an amazing opening issue for the series that will surely trap readers’ interest in reading more of the series. The mysteries that this issue either straight out tells us or implies are enough to peek even the most jaded readers’ interest. The premise that is laid out here in the first issue is intriguing, but when you know that Panosian obviously has more in store for us that jacks the intrigued levels all the way up. This should be a slam dunk pick up at the shop or Neon Ichiban this week. As a matter of fact, make sure to add this one to your Pull List as you won’t want to miss a single issue of this series.
The Dirt Beneath the Devil #1 is a solid debut issue. It takes a familiar concept and puts it in a setting that feels rather new and fresh.
G.I. Joe #25 is a major milestone done right, paying off years of buildup and kicking off the series' most epic storyline yet.

G.I. JOE #25 is a phenomenal start to the Nightforce story arc. Joshua Williamson, Tom Reilly and Andrea Milana pace things out that you feel like you are experiencing the start of a big blockbuster event. Everything that happens in this issue comes across as being a payoff for many sub-plots that have been developed since the start of the series. Where the payoff leads to is anyone’s guess, leaving you as the reader even more excited to find out what happens next.

Superman #40 is damn near perfect. This arc acted as a bit of a redemption for Superboy Prime and I absolutely adore him after this. Whilst the story here is wrapped up, this isn’t the last time we will see Superboy Prime and there seems to be a bright future ahead for him and his “supporting characters”.

This has been a phenomenal story setting up Prime’s future, but special credit once again goes to Dan Mora, who plays with the nature of the comic book format in some incredibly unique ways. The original Superman is back next month for the kickoff of the big “Kingdom of Zod” event, but I hope Williamson gets to keep writing Prime for a long time.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #300 (#20) not only pushes the great story that we have been following forward, but also gives this milestone issue a big feel as well. The drama, action, surprises, and emotions are firing on all cylinders in this issue. If this issue doesn’t make you feel something you may need to check your pulse. They could’ve just phoned this one in as the 300th issue milestone is more than enough to sell the book. But they didn’t phone it in at all and crafted an issue that is sure to bring readers back next month for issue 21. If Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles is not on your Pull List already it needs to be added ASAP! If you are a comic book collector this 300th issue needs to be added to your collection as well. Cheers to 300 issues of TMNT and can’t wait for the 400th milestone issue!

This issue takes you on an emotional ride! Sure there is plenty of action within these pages. All while tugging at your heart strings with the current situation revolving around Shen. Losing a loved one and having the chance to bring them back is going to hit home with many readers I suspect. You do not want to miss out on this start of a new storyline for this series of TMNT. Go get your copy today!

Operation: Iron Coffin #3 delivers a thrilling, blood-soaked finale that balances outrageous action with genuine emotional weight. Kenny Porter brings Dracula’s conflict with his children to a satisfying close, while Tyrell Cannon and Shawn Lee give the issue relentless visual energy. Brutal, heartfelt, and wildly entertaining, this is a fitting conclusion to the series. This has been one of my favorite series of the year and is one of the most entertaining series on the shelves. If for whatever reason you missed this one, try and get the issues at your LCS this week. If you can’t find them, definitely pick up the trade when it drops, so you don’t miss out on one of the best series of the year!

“Operation: Iron Coffin” is an absolute tour de force from start to finish. If you ever feel down about yourself, read this to remind yourself you’re so much more. If someone or something like Dracula can redeem himself, then so can we.

Operation: Iron Coffin #2 keeps the momentum going with a bigger, bloodier, and more personal chapter for Dracula. Kenny Porter deepens the story without slowing down the action, while Tyrell Cannon’s artwork delivers the chaos, horror, and energy this concept demands. This series continues to be an absolute blast and remains an easy Pull List recommendation. Do not sleep on this series! Make sure you jump on this train now, as you don’t want to miss what happens next.

I don’t know how they’re doing it, but “Operation: Iron Coffin” is one of the best out this year. Kenny Porter manages to create a version of Dracula that feels relatable yet horrifying. His writing coupled with Cannon’s fantastic artwork create a truly amazing reading experience.
One of the best series in comics right now. The art is wild, creative, adventurous, and stunning. The story keeps drawing you back in issue after issue.
Marc Spector: Moon Knight #7 delivers an exhilarating ride with huge action, incredible artwork, and deadly stakes. It leaves you itching for the next issue.

The Smart Division is a fantastic science-fiction mystery that eerily could be more fact than fiction. Writer Zack Kaplan delivers a timely detective tale exploring the use of modern technology in solving crimes. However, it’s the juxtaposition of John Pearson’s elegant brush strokes that makes story rise above the rest. Kaplan and Pearson’s creativity knows no bounds and The Smart Division is proof of that.

I sat down with The Smart Division expecting a slick sci-fi detective story and walked away rattled about the world outside my window. That is the highest thing I can say about a comic right now. This is a perfect debut and one of the most relevant books on the stands, and I cannot wait to see where the case goes.

King Shazam and Superman throw down in a final fight for the ages! Arron leaves it all on table with the script. The art team never knows a ceiling in how far to raise the stakes. Highest possible recommendation.

Absolute Superman #21 feels like a true spectacle and lives up to the hype in every way as this arc comes to. a close. There is so much violence, emotion, and power packed into these pages that it may, in fact, be my favorite issue of the run yet.
Superman: The Stranger #1 returns to Clark Kent's roots, spinning a story that shows why Superman is such a timeless character.

The best Superman comic I’ve read in years!  A 1930s reinvention of the Man of Steel that returns Superman to his 1930s roots, but zigs and zags in ways you won’t expect, while keeping you on your toes. With a story that hooks you from the go and art and colours that leap off the page, this is a must-read mini-series.

Six of Us #1 turns a seemingly perfect 1990s sitcom cast into a web of secrets, resentment, and murder, with Tom King and Gabriel Hernández Walta delivering a compelling mystery that leaves everyone looking potentially guilty.

SIX OF US reminds us why this award winning creative team is so unstoppable. It's a human story about the importance of creating art, but the cost of it too. Six of Us #1 invites us to consider what true fulfillment looks like, and whether it has anything to do with success.
Black Tower: The Raven Conspiracy #1 is a compelling mix of magic and spy fiction, packed with haunting imagery and a unique mystery.

Black Tower: The Raven Conspiracy #1 proves that everything out of DC Vertigo should be jumped on immediately. This was a strong start to a comic series that has captured my attention from the first page and didn’t let go until the ending. I cannot recommend this comic enough!

The Smart Division #2 will inject a level of fear into the reader that they may not have thought an issue could do. This may be a story, but, Zack, John, and Hassan blur the lines of reality, posing ethical questions regarding AI and leaving us with an ending that sinks us deeper into the mystery.

The Smart Division #2 builds confidently on the series’ opening mystery with sharper tension, compelling character conflict, and an unsettling exploration of AI and corporate power. Zack Kaplan keeps the investigation unpredictable, while John J. Pearson delivers immersive artwork that strengthens the book’s noir atmosphere. This is a smart, suspenseful second issue that leaves the case more dangerous and more intriguing than ever. If this series isn’t already on your Pull List, reconsider that decision NOW.

Erica’s return to present time brings forth a much needed encounter behind heavy drama. Tynion IV opens deep wounds with incredible writing. Dell’edera and Muerto craft the intense exchanges with superb art. No one does slow burn drama better than SIKTC!

Batman has to attempt a cold solution to Gotham City’s attack, but is he too late? Fraction successfully layers humorous scenes in the ever growing drama. Scalera and Morey dive into the wild scenarios unfolding in the pages. A nother unique look at the connection between The Dark Knight and his rogues.

Batman #14 is one of those rare event tie-ins that is both extremely important to the overall story (this feels like it’s the turning point in the war against the Green) but also doesn’t really feel like it’s a part of an event. Fraction is able to capture a human side of the Batman mythos that just does it for me and this issue has so much of that; Verity’s sarcasm sent me into paroxysms of laughter several times. Scalera and Morey’s art is flawless Bat-art and some of the best I’ve seen this year. Batman: Bad Seeds has slowly grew on me (I didn’t realize this was something of a pun until after I wrote it), because every part of it I’ve read has been great and this issue is no different.

Spawn #379 is all talk and no show when assorted side characters look for information. Matthew Rosenberg moves the players around to get ready for bigger events down the line, but if you skipped this issue, you’d miss nothing. Still, Stephen Segovia’s artwork saves the day.

Hyde Street #13 sheds light on The Butcher as he wreaks havoc on the residents of Hyde Street while shrouding his motivations in more mystery. If this issue is any indication, things are about to get far more intense.

The fundamental mystery of the street impression remains even though there's a bit a lot of backstory delivered about it. And there's a very clever eye towards exactly where the mysteries lie on the street. Johns is doing a very good job of casting light in select places in order to amplify the mystery of what's going on. And at the center of it all there's a lot of people who are really suffering. And about the heart of this series. But there is the mystery beyond it all. And that ends up being a lot of fun to think about.

The JSA covert mission sinks further behind enemy lines in a thrilling farewell chapter Lemire exposes the internal pull of being a hero with superb writing. Kristiansen shows true grit while the stakes get higher. A vintage look at a team that transcends time and history.

A series continues to be quite appealing. The big task of any writer long-term series is how well vacant integrate their story with a big crossover event. Brombal does a good job of advancing.Cass’ progression as a person while also allowing her the opportunity to fit perfectly into this a rather large and un wheeled crossover event.

Cassandra Cain’s valiant mission puts her life in danger with a thrilling new chapter. Brombal falls back into the heavy action themes with the writing. Miyazawa & Castro construct exciting moments in between the mounting drama. Cassandra Cain’s showing her growth as a hero in these pages.
Overall fun, compelling and pretty to look at, another great issue from the Sonic creative team and I look forward to seeing how this mini-arc wraps up.

The Deadman #5 sets us up for an explosive ending to the first arc of this incredible story. Boston’s journey has taken him to some weird places, and he must now face a foe who will not stop until everything is destroyed.

The future of Boston Brand is anything but linear as the Gr33n offers an assist. Prince continues to push boundaries with the writing. Morazzo & O'Halloran craft unforgettable looks while moving Brand thought the unknown. A story unlike anything else at the shops keeps its’ winning ways.

Crowbound #2 is a haunting, visually stunning continuation that transforms Rose into a terrifying force of vengeance. Dustin Nguyen's gorgeous watercolor artwork brings an unsettling beauty to the dystopian setting, particularly when Rose's newfound brutality takes center stage. The flashbacks occasionally overstate her motivations, but the Scarecrow Queen's mysterious influence and a creepy new threat leave plenty to anticipate.

It's nice to see this thing moving forward in a way that feels quite distinctly unlike any other sword and sorcery fantasy style narrative. That's on the rack today. There's a lot that piles into it that feels remarkably well articulated. And yet there isn't quite enough fresh originality in it to really capture the imagination quite yet. However, it is leaning off in a direction of being very compelling. And really it's only a matter of time before things really develop. It will be interesting to see where this goes in the future.

Zatanna #6 continues to bring some beautiful art, and is a magical addition to anyone’s pull list. The importance of community and coming plays a major part in solving their problem, and it ends on one hell of a tease for next time.

Zatanna #6 is a fast-paced and eventful issue that shows Zatanna’s growth while she tries to save the Hidden City. Jamal Campbell’s compelling writing paired with gorgeous visuals by himself, Andrew Dalhouse and Ariana Maher makes this an issue that was with the wait.

Superman The Stranger is quickly shaping up to be the Man of Steel equivalent of Frank Miller’s The Dark Knight Returns. It’s bold, unsettling, and challenges what readers expect from a Superman story with its noir spin and Craig and Wordie’s evocative art deco style. This is the Superman story you must read!

Superman sees a higher calling while helping the voiceless as the Golden Age reveals more dangers. Craig hones in on the weight of hope & vintage looks guiding the way. A vastly different take on the Man Of Steel mythos.

This was SUCH a good ending to this arc. How everything ended, how the characters handled the situations, and the pure emotions that ran throughout this issue, everything was beautifully handled. Gail Simone, Luciano Vecchio, Matthew Wilson, and Clayton Cowles should be very proud of themselves for this one.

The X-Men battle pure evil on two fronts in an exciting arc finale! Simone unleashes the fury behind heroic eyes with a fantastic script. Vecchio and Wilson craft intense images that never let up on the magnitude of the events. This run of UXM what you set the benchmark for modern X-Men stories to hit!

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Midnight Spider-Man #1 puts a horrifying spin on Peter Parker's origins, complete with compelling yet gruesome art and a deconstruction of his iconic principles about great power and great responsibility.
pros: Johnson skillfully deconstructs Spidey's mantra of great power and great responsibility in a way that fits the Midnight Universe.
ScieTronc's artwork feels anime-inspired, and also ramps up the body horror.
Neeraj Menon's color work paints gore in vivid showers.
Plenty of characters from the Spider-Man mythos get reworked in surprising ways.
An ending that will leave you with chills.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Midnight X-Men #1 proves Jonathan Hickman still knows exactly how to make the X-Men feel dangerously unpredictable.
pros: Hickman immediately establishes an intriguing new status quo for the X-Men
The competing factions create plenty of mystery and potential conflict
Matteo Della Fonte’s detailed, realistic artwork makes the horror hit hard
cons: The larger world could use a little more definition
Action is relatively limited until the final third

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Midnight Fantastic Four #1 is a horrifying and menacing start to this darker take on Marvel's First Family, and serves as a great statement for the possibility of the Midnight line.
pros: Feels unique and fresh instead of just making our heroes into villains
Benjamin Percy's script does a great job of placing a sense of dread just below the surface of the story, so we know something bad will happen but we don't know…
Kev Walker's art is truly surprising in this, both in what he accomplishes gore wise and horror
Midnight Reed Richards might be one of the most sympathetic takes on the character I've ever read
Sets up a lot of interesting long term seeds for the title in the future
cons: Ben and Johnny don't have as much to do in this opening story as Reed and Sue

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Superman: The Stranger #2 starts to take some big swings, while also remembering the core concepts of what makes a great Superman story. This might be a Black Label book, but it definitely has the shining heart of Superman.
pros: Craig understands that Lois Lane should be an important part of any Superman story.
The art continues to capture that big, bold Golden Age energy.
Vibrant colors that make Metropolis feel like a living dream and nightmare.
cons: The Luthor parts seem to re-tread elements from the first issue.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Absolute Superman #24 shines thanks to the spotlight it puts on Steel, as John Henry Irons becomes the Man of Steel's most stalwart ally. Next issue is the landmark Absolute Superman #25, and I trust Aaron to deliver a truly epic story.
pros: Aaron delivers a surprisingly sincere story that puts the spotlight on Steel.
Ferrerya fills up splash pages with truly terrifying villains and epic fight scenes.
Steel gets an extremely cool makeover.
The stage is set for an epic showdown in next issue.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Jonah Hex and the Shadow of Death #1 is an perfect jumping-on point for new readers, as it delivers the best of the classic Western genre and infuses it with superb horror.
pros: Walsh's script beautifully merges a Western story about a gunslinger with supernatural elements and adds in bone-chilling horror.
As a huge fan of "Logan" and "Red Dead Redemption", seeing these influences captured so perfectly on the page was a fun reading experience.
Griffin perfectly complementsWalsh's art; the purple shades for the night sky are a fitting choice, and other subdued colors add to the classic Western vibe.
Carey's lettering is outstanding as well, with dynamic sound effects for creaking on the floor and gunshots making the story feel alive.
cons: The issue could be too new-reader friendly; hardcore fans may be looking for more ties to Jonah Hex's past, whereas there are only references here and there.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: The Demon #1 is an excellent showcase for James Harren, whose monster designs and expressive storytelling make Gotham feel infested with supernatural danger. Keeping Etrigan largely restrained gives Jason Blood room to establish himself as a capable, compelling lead, while glimpses of ancient history suggest Harren has much bigger plans for both characters. The mythology can be difficult to parse…
pros: Harren's monster designs are imaginative, creepy, and frequently funny
Jason Blood gets a surprisingly strong spotlight
Holding Etrigan back makes his appearances feel more significant
cons: Some of the mythology and backstory are difficult to understand this early
Readers expecting a lot of Etrigan may be surprised by his limited presence

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Batman #14 is a confusing mess that relies on threads that readers are expected to have picked up on from Detective Comics.
pros: The banter between Bruce and Verity Pennyworth is hilarious.
The backup story is really interesting.
cons: Prior reading outside of this series is required to know what's going on, which makes this a disruption in the series lacking proper flow.
The opening to this issue makes zero sense as to why people are suddenly breaking into Pennyworth Manor.
The added conflict between Victor and Nora Fries feels cumbersome.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: The Deadman #5 has a ton of great ideas packed into a very short ride. The future DC concepts, morality questions, and clever callbacks make this an enjoyable chapter. Still, I couldn’t shake the feeling that Prince had enough material here for a much deeper story. With the first arc coming to a close, I’m still invested in seeing where Boston Brand’s strange journey leads, and hopefully the final…
pros: Creative techno-futuristic DC world with fun reimaginings of familiar characters and concepts
Strong exploration of karma and morality with interesting questions about Deadman’s role as “Custodian of All Souls”
Excellent Morazzo/O’Halloran visuals
cons: Moves too quickly, as several intriguing ideas needed more development
Some future characters and concepts feel more like teases than fully realized pieces of the story

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Mike Costa, Ryan Browne, and Brian Kolek mash up two properties like kids playing with a turnover. The Kaiju of Oz is a fun read, but doesn't provide anything beneath the surface.
pros: Mike Costa and Brian Kolek make sure the book is full of visual gags.
Ryan Browne's artwork is really fantastic, combining both properties visually in this subversive fantasy.
cons: At a certain point, you just expect the story to have something to say, and this book never really gets there. For these two properties, that's disappointing.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Zatanna #6 is a fast-paced and eventful issue that shows Zatanna’s growth while she tries to save the Hidden City. Jamal Campbell’s compelling writing paired with gorgeous visuals by himself, Andrew Dalhouse and Ariana Maher makes this an issue that was with the wait.
pros: Ariana Maher’s letters make this issue easy and entertaining to read.
Jamal Campbell’s slow building of the world of magic places certain scenes and spells Zatanna uses into context without over explaining.
Campbell’s artwork and they way he uses different panels makes for visually interesting but gorgeous pages
cons: I wish we knew more about Atik’s motives other than he was ignored.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: The Smart Division #2 is sharp techno-noir, with stylish layouts and an interesting premise. However, the second issue doesn't quite live up to the promise of the first, losing momentum in the issue's closing act.
pros: John J. Pearson's layouts provide a lot of depth to the story, creating interesting visual moments.
Writer Zack Kaplan and letterer Buddy Beaudoin do a great job with the beats of the dialogue.
cons: This issue lacks the urgency of the debut.
The ending here veers a bit too close to the ending of the debut to feel novel.
